Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Senegal has active use of digitized payments in public programs/services: the SEN-CSU (universal health coverage agency) implemented a plan to digitalize operations and payments nationwide and reports significant results, indicating ongoing government-linked digital disbursements/collections for health coverage processes. ([Better Than Cash Alliance case study on SEN-CSU](https://www.betterthancash.org/explore-resources/how-has-senegal-made-responsible-digital-payments-a-catalyst-for-universal-health-coverage))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Limited Use to Yes - Active Use. The official Trésor Public site confirms SenTrésor (launched 2 June 2025 by the Minister of Finance, piloted from 28 March 2025) digitises G2P disbursements — salaries, pensions, scholarships and social assistance — via mobile money nationwide, serving over 44,000 beneficiaries and disbursing ~CFA4bn by launch, alongside the pre-existing SEN-CSU health-premium digitisation. Confirmed via an official government source rather than the single NGO case study originally cited.

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Person-to-government payments (fees/premiums) are supported through SEN-CSU’s SUNUCSU app, which integrates Orange Money, Wave, Free Money and e-banking to pay membership/premium fees digitally. ([SUNUCSU app listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sunucsu.mobile))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Limited Use to Yes - Active Use. Official Trésor and DGID (tax authority) sources confirm an established télépaiement system (ADIE TELEDAC + DGID E-TAX/eTax) for online declaration and payment of taxes, duties and fees, with mandatory digital VAT filing/payment for qualifying taxpayers since July 2024. This is active, government-wide use, not merely the limited use implied by the single SUNUCSU app listing originally cited.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Central Bank (BCEAO) directly manages/operates SICA-UEMOA (automated retail clearing) and STAR-UEMOA (RTGS), including supervision, incident handling, reporting and invoicing, under WAEMU Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU. ([BCEAO – Payment Systems Management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at Direct Operation. BCEAO's own site and Instruction No. 001-01-2024 (2024/2025, applicable to Senegal as a UEMOA member) corroborate that the central bank directly manages and operates SICA-UEMOA (retail clearing) and STAR-UEMOA (RTGS) under WAEMU Regulation 15/2002/CM/WAMU. Score unchanged; second authoritative source now confirms it.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Senegal’s 2022–2026 National Financial Inclusion Strategy includes a pillar focused on “protection of users of financial services” and establishing a national mechanism coordinating financial education and consumer protection, indicating a formal consumer-protection policy framework linked to DFS/payments (though not a stand-alone payments ombuds scheme was evidenced in sources collected). ([AFI – Senegal’s 2022–2026 NFIS](https://afi-global.org/publication/senegals-2022-2026-national-financial-inclusion-strategy/))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Partial to Yes. BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 relative aux services de paiement dans l'UMOA (in force from January 2025, applicable to Senegal as a UEMOA member state) contains a dedicated Chapter VII 'Protection des utilisateurs de services de paiement', with specific provisions such as Article 48 on safeguarding of user funds — a payment-specific consumer protection regime going beyond the general inclusion-strategy pillar that was the sole original source.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: BCEAO states it compiles and releases regular reports related to payment systems under its management (SICA-UEMOA/STAR-UEMOA), but the research run did not locate a public monthly/quarterly dashboard with downloadable time series specific to Senegal; evidence supports at least ad-hoc/regular reporting. ([BCEAO – Payment Systems Management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Upgraded from Ad Hoc to Annual. BCEAO publishes a recurring statistical report, 'Rapport sur les Infrastructures de Marchés Financiers, les Moyens et les Services de Paiement', covering SICA-UEMOA/STAR-UEMOA (which includes Senegal), with editions for 2016, 2017, 2020-2021 and 2022-2023, disclosing transaction volumes/values and participant counts. This is a regular, institutionalised publication (now roughly biennial) rather than merely ad hoc, though not monthly/quarterly.

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: Senegal’s 2022–2026 National Financial Inclusion Strategy explicitly targets vulnerable segments (women, youth, rural populations, SMEs) and includes Pillar II focused on developing digital financial services infrastructure to underpin G2P payments, plus Pillar III on user protection/financial education mechanisms. ([AFI – Senegal’s 2022–2026 NFIS](https://afi-global.org/publication/senegals-2022-2026-national-financial-inclusion-strategy/))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Provisionally confirmed at Yes but flagged for human review. The full official SNIF 2022-2026 document (DGSFC) shows explicit governance structures (Conseil National; Comité de Coordination et de Suivi) and an explicit mandate on financial culture/consumer protection targeting vulnerable groups (women, youth, rural populations, SMEs/MSMEs), meeting the 'explicit financial inclusion mandate in a governance document' clause. However, no evidence was found of payment-scheme-specific governance mechanisms (e.g. reserved board seats for consumer or small-PSP representatives within SICA-UEMOA/STAR-UEMOA governance) — the NFIS is a broader financial-inclusion strategy rather than payment-system governance per se, so a human should confirm this fits the variable's intent.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: High digital payments uptake evidenced by GSMA-cited BCEAO data: 76% of Senegal’s adult population has a mobile money account, and in 2024 Senegal had 14.65 million active accounts. This implies >70% user penetration (score band 70–89%). ([Ecofin Agency report citing BCEAO via GSMA](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news/0812-51194-gsma-maps-the-reforms-required-for-senegal-s-digital-takeoff))
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at 70-89%. Cross-checked against a second independent primary source: World Bank Global Findex 2025 microdata (fieldwork 2024) shows 72.6% of Senegalese adults hold a mobile money account, corroborating the GSMA/BCEAO-cited 76% figure and 14.65m active accounts in 2024. Both sit within the 70-89% band, resolving the original single-source flag. Note the underlying metric is account ownership/active-account count rather than a strict 90-day-active-user survey, but no better-matched dataset was found.
